items.title: Subtitle Placement
items.summary: Implementing these rules will reduce visual distraction, ensuring that subtitles are only shown where they are most useful and least obtrusive. This improves user experience by maintaining a clean frame while still providing critical information during interactions.
items.probe: Define one fixed subtitle position rule for V1: keep subtitles at the bottom center of the display.

choices.label: More Prominent
choices.description: Bias toward easier visibility over subtlety.

items.title: Confidence Display
items.summary: A well-defined confidence display will help users understand the reliability of the system's output, leading to increased trust and better usage in noisy or challenging environments where accurate real-time subtitles are critical.
items.probe: Choose one confidence display format for V1: label only or label plus short reason.

choices.label: Label Only
choices.description: Keep certainty display minimal and fast to parse.

choices.label: Label + Reason
choices.description: Expose a short reason to improve trust.

items.title: Memory/Cache Policy
items.summary: By automatically reinforcing new people in memory, the system will show increased accuracy and reliability when recalling names and faces, which strengthens trust and utility without adding complexity.
items.probe: Set one local cache eviction rule for face/name memory in V1.

choices.label: Smaller Cache
choices.description: Bias toward tighter local memory and lower load.

choices.label: Recency First
choices.description: Bias toward recent names and conversations.

items.title: Phone/Cloud Boundary
items.summary: By focusing V1 on clear, reliable real-time subtitles, we can build trust with users early. This will allow us to iterate on richer memory and confidence features without initial processing delays or battery concerns. Users will experience consistent, usable subtitle assistance right from the start.
items.probe: Choose one phone-local versus cloud fallback boundary for face/name recall lookup in V1.

choices.label: Phone First
choices.description: Keep critical work local unless clearly necessary.

choices.label: Balanced Fallback
choices.description: Allow cloud assist for slower or richer lookups.

items.title: Visual Hierarchy
items.summary: By prioritizing subtitles in the visual hierarchy, we can enhance the wearer's ability to focus on critical information during live interactions, reducing cognitive load and improving overall understanding without overwhelming them with too much visual data. This will help maintain trust and usability by ensuring that the most important content is always at the forefront.
items.probe: Define the visual hierarchy rule where subtitles are given higher prominence over one-line support during live interactions.

choices.label: Subtitles Dominate
choices.description: Keep subtitles above all other overlays.

choices.label: Balanced Overlay
choices.description: Allow prompts to share attention more evenly.
